newsitem.title: UK: Ldn freight - Capers in demand, Panamaxes less so.
newsitem.headline: Ldn freight - Capers in demand, Panamaxes less so.

text.p: Capers found good demand from minerals charterers but Panamax levels, more dependent on grain especially in the Atlantic, looked vulnerable in the opinion of some brokers.

These influences negated each other and produced an unchanged BFI at 1511. Geared tonnage may be enjoying steadier conditions in the Far East - which pushed the Baltic Handy Index up 10 to 1022 - But the current situation for average Handies continues to deteriorate in the US Gulf and E Coast S America.

Charterers' brokers believe there are few Panamax stems remaining for Jan shipment and that consequently the nearby positions in the Atlantic are softening. No fixtures were reported in this category Tuesday with most activity being concentrated in the falling Handy sector. Dreyfus were reported to have booked a vessel for 28000 tonnes 53' Paranagua to Rotterdam for Jan 20/27 at a lumpsum equivalent of a significantly lower $16.00, and Romac were linked with the 1973-built Arabella 26,510 dwt delivery prompt Recalada trip Turkey at a very economical $6,750 daily plus $75,000 bonus.

New orders included Klaveness with 60,000/5 heavy grain Mississippi/ARA for Feb 5/15 and Egyptian charterers for a Panamax delivery plate in February trip Egyptian Med. Reports leaked out of last week's fixture by Toepfer of Periandros of Korinthos for about 100,000 barley from N France and possibly Antwerp to Jeddah for Jan 20/30 at $20.50.

In the Pacific Militos 65,000 dwt was fixed by Hanjin delivery NoPac trip S Korea for end Jan loading at $10,500 daily plus $197,500 bonus. There were rumours that Hanjin also fixed Baltic Mermaid 64,145 dwt for a NoPac round at $11,000 daily. Bunge fixed 20,500 wheat Vancouver/2 ports Brazil for Jan 20/30 at about $26/26.25.

Capers were again in demand. Hokkaido Star was said to be closely working Rohstoffhandel for 160,000 ironore Tubarao/Rotterdam for Feb 15/28 at over $6.00, Kalahari 161,000 dwt was believed fixed by COE and Clerici delivery Continent for a trip via Norfolk with Coal to Brazil, but Cetragpa's fixture of 120,000 coal Richards Bay/Milaki for Feb 1/15 may have failed on subjects. New Harvest was still on subjects for 200,000/10 ironore Tubarao/Japan for Feb 15/2at a strong $10.50 with Bocimar, as was Lassia for 130,000 ironore Saldanha/Beilun for mid Feb at $8.00 with Rod Holdings.

SCF Trust 96,000 dwt was linked with P and O for coal from Hampton Roads to Rotterdam for mid/end Jan shipment at $6.50. Merchant Paramount was believed to have failed on subjects with BHP for about 150,000 coal Queensland/Taranto at $10.40. In the Panamaxes Atlantica 64,000 dwt failed on subjects with UBT delivery Black Sea trip with fertilizers to China, and the geared Ektor 64,285 dwt was fixed for steels from Black Sea to Thailand at a reported level of between $17,500 and 18,000 daily. K Line agreed $16,000 daily for an unnamed vessel for ironore from Narvik to Cigading on subjects.

A number of fixtures were undisclosed because of secrecy clauses. A 1976-built 34,000 dwt vessel fixed delivery Plate for 3-5 months at about $7,250 daily plus $150,000 bonus, and Sea Harmony was reported taken by Cargill for 30,000 fertilizers Tampa/India for prompt loading at $35.00.
